leo1.text: [whispers] Take Leo. It's one in the morning, [pause] and someone on the internet is wrong.

leo2.text: [mischievously] So he types the perfect comeback. [quickly] Type. Post. Win.

leo3.text: [sighs] By morning: two hundred replies. [pause] Not one about his point. [dramatically] All about his logic.

cold1.text: [serious] Leo isn't alone. Every day, billions of us post, comment and reply, [pause] and almost nobody checks their own reasoning.

mit.text: [gravely] On Twitter, false stories were seventy percent more likely to be retweeted than true ones.

wef.text: [ominous] And in 2024, and again in 2025, the World Economic Forum ranked misinformation the number one global risk for the next two years.

pivot.text: [intensely] We have spell-check. We have grammar-check. [long pause] But nothing checks our logic.

vision.text: [hopeful] What if something caught the flaw in your argument, [pause] before the whole world did?

intro.text: [confident] Meet Ember, your critical thinking partner: a Chrome extension that reads only what you write, and flags fallacies right where they happen.

d1.text: [calm] It ignores everything you read. [pause] It only watches what you type.

d2.text: [suspenseful] Slip into a fallacy, and it's tagged right on the words that did it.

d3.text: [amused] Subtle, it is not. [pause] Every flag lands with drama, so you can't miss it.

d4.text: Click the tag: Claude explains why, and asks one question to make your argument stronger. [pause] Fix it, and the flag clears.

science.text: [confident] It knows twenty-six classic fallacies, [pause] and stays quiet when your reasoning holds.

privacy.text: [warmly] It reads your words, never your feed: [pause] no passwords, no pasted text, nothing you didn't write yourself.

impact.text: For students, for work, for anyone in a comment section: [pause] every message becomes a chance to think twice.

outro.text: [warmly] Ember. [pause] Catch the fallacy. [pause] Keep the argument.
